description: We are a team of passionate Aerospace Engineering students from Universiti Sains Malaysia, eager to gain experience and contribute to the advancement of the aerospace industry.
summary:
ORBYX is an interactive space mission simulation game that makes aerospace engineering and space exploration accessible and enjoyable for everyone, even those with no prior scientific knowledge.

The game features four progressive missions: Earth observation, lunar exploration and return, emergency evacuation, and planetary exploration. Players can play solo or collaborate in teams of up to four. They explore spacecraft environments, complete tasks and make engineering decisions while managing resources such as mass, power, fuel, propulsion and communications. Each decision affects the mission's outcome, helping players understand how spacecraft systems work together. Mission results are saved so players can review their performance and learn from previous attempts.

ORBYX addresses the challenge by turning complex space mission design concepts into an interactive, hands-on experience. Rather than simply reading about engineering trade-offs, players learn through experimentation, problem-solving and gameplay.

Our goal is to spark curiosity about aerospace, astronomy and space exploration, especially among younger generations and people unfamiliar with these fields. By combining science with storytelling, exploration and teamwork, ORBYX shows that learning about space can be both educational and fun.
details:
ORBYX is an interactive educational space mission game designed to introduce players to the fascinating world of space exploration, aerospace engineering and astronomy through an enjoyable gaming experience. The main idea behind the project is to make space mission design more accessible to everyone, including people who have little or no prior knowledge of space science or engineering.

Rather than learning these concepts through complex theories and equations alone, players get to explore, experiment and make engineering decisions while playing a game. Through this approach, we aim to help players understand important space mission parameters such as spacecraft mass, power consumption, propulsion, fuel requirements, communication systems, orbital selection, scientific instruments and resource management, as well as how these factors influence one another.

How Does It Work?

ORBYX consists of four progressive missions, each introducing different challenges and engineering concepts. As players advance through the levels, the missions become increasingly challenging, requiring more planning, teamwork and decision-making.

Level 1 – Earthwatch (Easy)

Players take on the role of a space mission team responsible for preparing an Earth-observation satellite. They must configure the spacecraft by selecting suitable components and managing parameters such as mass, power, payload capacity and communications. The objective is to ensure that the satellite is properly configured to complete its observation mission.

Level 2 – Lunar Survey and Return (Intermediate)

Players progress to a lunar exploration mission, where they must prepare a spacecraft to travel to the Moon, conduct scientific observations and return safely. This mission introduces more demanding considerations, including propulsion, fuel requirements, orbital manoeuvres, thermal management, scientific data collection and communication with Earth.

Level 3 – Emergency Evacuation (Hard)

The story takes an unexpected turn when a spacecraft experiences an emergency involving a dangerous alien organism. Players must work together to manage the damaged spacecraft, contain the threat and prepare individual escape vehicles. Each astronaut's survival depends on the engineering decisions made when configuring their escape vehicle and managing its available resources.

Level 4 – Project Lazarus (Extreme)

In the final mission, players embark on an ambitious planetary exploration expedition. They must manage limited shared resources while exploring different planetary environments, collecting scientific evidence and ensuring that the crew can return safely. Different environmental conditions create additional challenges, requiring players to consider factors such as radiation exposure, temperature, energy consumption, oxygen supplies and available return resources. At the end, players evaluate their findings and collectively decide which planetary candidate deserves further investigation.

Throughout the game, players interact with different engineering stations, make decisions between available configurations and observe how their choices affect mission performance. The game also provides mission evaluations and explanations to help players understand the consequences of their decisions.

Gameplay Modes and Mission Progress :

ORBYX supports both individual and team gameplay. Players can take on missions independently and make their own engineering decisions, or collaborate with other players as a team to plan, manage resources, solve problems and complete mission objectives.

After each mission, the game saves the mission results and performance report. Players can revisit these records at a later time to review their decisions, examine mission outcomes, identify mistakes and understand how different engineering choices affected the mission. This allows learning to continue beyond a single playthrough and encourages players to experiment with different strategies and improve their designs.

By combining solo exploration, team collaboration and saved mission reviews, ORBYX offers a flexible learning experience that encourages both independent thinking and teamwork.

Benefits and Educational Value

One of the main benefits of ORBYX is that it makes aerospace and space science concepts accessible to people from different educational backgrounds. Players do not need to be aerospace engineering students or have previous knowledge of orbital mechanics to participate.

By presenting engineering concepts through interactive gameplay, players can learn while exploring, experimenting and enjoying the experience. Instead of simply being told that increasing spacecraft mass affects propulsion requirements, for example, they can experience how that decision influences the mission themselves.

The game also encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, resource management and decision-making. Players learn that successful space missions require different subsystems to work together and that improving one aspect of a spacecraft may introduce limitations elsewhere.

Intended Impact

Our main intention is to encourage more people, particularly younger generations and students, to develop an interest in aerospace engineering, astronomy and space exploration.

We hope ORBYX can serve as an introductory platform that sparks curiosity among people who may never have considered pursuing these fields. By combining education with an entertaining gaming experience, we want to demonstrate that space science is not limited to textbooks, advanced laboratories or professional scientists. It can also be explored through creativity, experimentation and interactive learning.

Ultimately, we hope the project contributes to greater awareness and enthusiasm for space exploration and inspires more young people to discover opportunities in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM).

Tools and Technologies Used

ORBYX was developed as a browser-based game using software development tools and web technologies.

- Programming languages: TypeScript and JavaScript.
- Web technologies: HTML and CSS.
- Game development framework: Phaser, used for the game environment, character movement, interactions, maps and gameplay mechanics.
- Multiplayer technology: PeerJS and WebRTC, used for the peer-to-peer multiplayer implementation.
- Development tools: Visual Studio Code and web browser development tools.
- Data storage: Browser-based local storage for player profiles, saved progress and mission records.

No dedicated physical hardware was required. The game was developed primarily as a software-based project intended to run on computers through a web browser.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ORBYX lies in combining aerospace engineering education with an interactive adventure game.

Our team developed the mission concepts, storylines, engineering challenges, planetary exploration scenarios and learning objectives through our own brainstorming and research. We also incorporated real-world space exploration references, including historical astronauts and their contributions to human spaceflight, to connect the fictional gameplay experience with actual achievements in space exploration.

The game features six astronaut characters inspired by historical space explorers, allowing players to learn about their backgrounds and contributions while participating in fictional missions.

We took inspiration from the gameplay style of the popular game Among Us, particularly its top-down character movement, exploration of different rooms and interactive task-based gameplay. We also adapted elements of an existing Among Us-style clone project as a starting point for parts of the game implementation. However, the ORBYX mission concepts, storylines, engineering challenges, gameplay progression and educational content were developed by our team. We wanted to create an experience that combines the excitement of an adventure game with the curiosity of scientific exploration. By introducing elements such as alien encounters, emergency evacuations and planetary expeditions alongside real engineering concepts, we aim to make learning about space more engaging and memorable.

Factors Considered During Development

Several factors were considered when developing ORBYX:

1. Accessibility: The game should be understandable and enjoyable even for players without an aerospace or science background.

2. Educational value: Engineering concepts should be introduced through gameplay and simple explanations rather than overwhelming players with complicated technical information.

3. Scientific relevance: Mission scenarios and engineering decisions should be connected to real space mission concepts and physical constraints, even when simplified for gameplay.

4. Gameplay and engagement: The game should remain entertaining through exploration, interactive tasks, storytelling, increasing difficulty and unexpected challenges.

5. Engineering trade-offs: Major decisions should have consequences for other spacecraft systems and mission resources, demonstrating the interconnected nature of space mission design.

6. Teamwork and collaboration: The missions are designed to encourage communication, shared responsibilities and collective decision-making, with support for up to four players.

7. Development limitations: As the project was developed within the limited time available during the hackathon, we prioritised building a playable experience covering all four missions while balancing technical complexity and development time.

Project Status

ORBYX is currently a working prototype. Although the four mission environments and their main gameplay and engineering mechanics have been developed, certain features, particularly multiplayer functionality and some additional interactions, have not yet undergone complete testing across different devices and network environments due to time constraints.

Further development and testing would be required to improve reliability, complete feature validation and expand the overall gaming experience.
